stem: A team wants employees to sign in to several cloud business applications with one organizational identity. Which service is the foundation?

choices.A: Azure Policy
choices.B: Microsoft Entra ID
choices.C: Microsoft Entra Domain Services
choices.D: Azure RBAC

explanations.A: Policy applies resource governance rules rather than providing a directory.
explanations.B: Entra ID supplies cloud identity and application sign-in.
explanations.C: A managed legacy domain is not the foundation for modern cloud-app sign-in.
explanations.D: RBAC authorizes Azure resource actions rather than supplying cloud sign-in identities.

stem: A legacy application requires LDAP and Kerberos in Azure, but the team does not want to maintain domain controllers. Which choice fits?

choices.A: Microsoft Entra Domain Services
choices.B: Microsoft Entra ID alone
choices.C: Self-managed AD DS on Azure VMs
choices.D: Microsoft Entra External ID customer tenant

explanations.A: The managed domain supports these legacy protocols.
explanations.B: Entra ID alone does not provide the application's traditional LDAP domain requirement.
explanations.C: That preserves legacy protocols but leaves the customer maintaining the domain controllers.
explanations.D: A customer sign-in design does not provide the required managed legacy domain.

stem: What does a Microsoft Entra tenant represent?

choices.A: An Azure subscription
choices.B: A management group
choices.C: A resource group
choices.D: A dedicated directory instance for identities and applications

explanations.A: A subscription is a resource and billing boundary, not the directory instance.
explanations.B: A management group organizes subscriptions rather than acting as the identity directory.
explanations.C: A resource group organizes Azure resources rather than the directory's identities.
explanations.D: The tenant is an identity boundary with its own directory objects.

stem: Who maintains the domain controllers provided by Microsoft Entra Domain Services?

choices.A: The customer's application development team
choices.B: The customer's VM guest-OS administrator
choices.C: The customer's directory infrastructure team
choices.D: Microsoft

explanations.A: The developers maintain their application, not the provider-managed domain controllers.
explanations.B: Domain Services provides its own managed controllers rather than customer-managed VM controllers.
explanations.C: That would describe self-managed domain controllers rather than this managed service.
explanations.D: The service manages its domain controllers.

stem: An architect needs Group Policy support for a migrated domain-dependent application. Which service should be evaluated?

choices.A: Microsoft Entra External ID
choices.B: Microsoft Entra Domain Services
choices.C: Microsoft Entra ID alone
choices.D: Azure Policy

explanations.A: External-app identity scenarios do not provide the required Group Policy domain service.
explanations.B: Managed domains provide Group Policy capabilities.
explanations.C: Modern cloud identity alone does not supply traditional Group Policy for this legacy-domain requirement.
explanations.D: Azure resource governance and traditional domain Group Policy are different mechanisms.

stem: Which requirement favors modern Microsoft Entra ID integration over a managed legacy domain?

choices.A: A migrated application requiring LDAP
choices.B: Signing in to a cloud application using modern identity protocols
choices.C: An application requiring NTLM
choices.D: A workload depending on domain Group Policy

explanations.A: A legacy LDAP requirement favors a compatible domain service rather than modern integration alone.
explanations.B: Modern cloud sign-in fits Entra ID without introducing a legacy domain.
explanations.C: NTLM compatibility is a traditional-domain use case.
explanations.D: Traditional Group Policy is a managed-domain capability.

stem: A learner sees the same tenant ID on two Azure subscriptions. What is a reasonable interpretation?

choices.A: The subscriptions must be the same billing container
choices.B: Both subscriptions must use the same Azure region
choices.C: Every user has identical access to both subscriptions
choices.D: Both subscriptions trust the same Entra directory

explanations.A: A shared tenant does not merge subscription boundaries.
explanations.B: Tenant association does not determine deployment regions.
explanations.C: Azure role assignments still determine access.
explanations.D: Multiple subscriptions can be associated with one tenant.

stem: Where should a team manage the source identity for a user synchronized into an Entra managed domain?

choices.A: Change the resource group's ownership tags
choices.B: Edit Azure RBAC assignments to change the user's directory profile
choices.C: Edit only the synchronized user inside the managed domain
choices.D: In the upstream identity source

explanations.A: Resource metadata does not maintain directory user objects.
explanations.B: Resource role assignments do not maintain directory profile attributes.
explanations.C: That does not update the upstream source of the synchronized identity.
explanations.D: Synchronized identities flow from Entra ID and any configured upstream directory.

stem: Which pairing correctly separates an identity directory from an Azure resource container?

choices.A: Entra tenant for identities; resource group for related Azure resources
choices.B: Management group for passwords; resource group for guest invitations
choices.C: VNet for application users; tenant for subnet prefixes
choices.D: Subscription for identities; tenant for virtual networks

explanations.A: The two containers solve different management problems.
explanations.B: Neither container replaces the directory's identity management.
explanations.C: VNets organize network addresses rather than directory users.
explanations.D: A subscription and tenant have resource and identity purposes respectively.

stem: What is the usual synchronization direction from Entra ID into Microsoft Entra Domain Services?

choices.A: From Azure Advisor into Entra ID
choices.B: From the managed domain to every Azure subscription
choices.C: Bidirectionally for every object without restrictions
choices.D: From Entra ID to the managed domain

explanations.A: Advisor is not an identity synchronization source.
explanations.B: Subscriptions are not synchronized directories.
explanations.C: The managed domain is not unrestricted bidirectional synchronization.
explanations.D: The managed domain receives synchronized identity information.

stem: A learner can authenticate to Azure but cannot list resources in a subscription. What should they distinguish?

choices.A: Authentication and DNS replication
choices.B: Subscription location and storage tier
choices.C: Tenant creation and disk sizing
choices.D: Directory authentication and resource authorization

explanations.A: DNS replication does not grant resource access.
explanations.B: These are unrelated to authorization.
explanations.C: Neither explains the permission decision.
explanations.D: A recognized identity still needs permission at an appropriate resource scope.

stem: Which capability is associated with a traditional managed domain?

choices.A: Domain join for compatible virtual machines
choices.B: Providing object-storage lifecycle rules
choices.C: Replacing all application authorization logic
choices.D: Automatically deploying every Azure resource

explanations.A: Domain Services supports domain-dependent workloads.
explanations.B: Lifecycle rules are a storage capability.
explanations.C: Applications and resource permissions still require access design.
explanations.D: Resource deployment is a separate management function.

stem: Which statement about Entra ID and self-managed Active Directory Domain Services is accurate?

choices.A: Entra ID is a managed implementation of every AD DS protocol
choices.B: Entra ID requires a customer-deployed controller for each tenant
choices.C: They serve different identity scenarios and can be integrated
choices.D: AD DS and Entra ID cannot participate in a hybrid identity design

explanations.A: Cloud identity and traditional AD DS have different protocol capabilities.
explanations.B: The cloud identity directory is a managed service.
explanations.C: Cloud identity and traditional domain services have distinct capabilities.
explanations.D: Organizations can integrate directory identity with appropriate synchronization and authentication design.

stem: An organization plans to use Entra Domain Services. What should be included in its design?

choices.A: A suitable Azure network and managed-domain requirements
choices.B: Assume it is equivalent to adding a free directory tag
choices.C: Use it instead of modern sign-in for every new cloud app
choices.D: Grant every workload subscription Owner for domain sign-in

explanations.A: The managed domain is a deployed service with network and cost considerations.
explanations.B: A managed domain is a deployed service with network and cost implications.
explanations.C: A legacy-domain requirement should guide selection rather than blanket replacement.
explanations.D: Azure resource ownership is not a universal domain authentication requirement.

stem: Which observation from az account show helps identify the subscription's directory association?

choices.A: id
choices.B: tenantId
choices.C: name
choices.D: state

explanations.A: The id field identifies the subscription, not its tenant association.
explanations.B: This field identifies the associated Entra tenant.
explanations.C: The subscription display name is not its directory identifier.
explanations.D: The state indicates whether the subscription is enabled rather than its tenant identity.

stem: A supplier needs access to one enterprise application using their existing work identity. Which capability fits?

choices.A: Microsoft Entra Domain Services
choices.B: B2B collaboration in Microsoft Entra External ID
choices.C: Azure RBAC alone
choices.D: Customer identity in an external tenant

explanations.A: A legacy managed domain is not the required partner collaboration design.
explanations.B: B2B supports collaboration with business guests.
explanations.C: Resource roles do not establish the supplier's external sign-in identity relationship.
explanations.D: That targets customer-app sign-up rather than workforce partner collaboration.

stem: A company is building sign-up and sign-in for retail customers. Which identity scenario should it evaluate?

choices.A: B2B invitations for workforce collaboration
choices.B: Azure RBAC accounts for every shopper
choices.C: Microsoft Entra Domain Services
choices.D: Customer identity and access management in an external tenant

explanations.A: This is a consumer-app identity scenario rather than inviting business partners to workforce apps.
explanations.B: Resource-management authorization is not consumer-app identity management.
explanations.C: A managed legacy domain is not the normal retail-customer sign-up design.
explanations.D: External tenants support consumer-facing application identities.

stem: What should an invited business guest receive?

choices.A: Access to every employee application after invitation
choices.B: Permanent directory administration rights
choices.C: Permissions appropriate to the collaboration task
choices.D: Automatic Reader access to every subscription in the tenant

explanations.A: The approved collaboration task should determine application access.
explanations.B: A business guest invitation does not justify directory administration.
explanations.C: Guest access should follow least privilege.
explanations.D: Even a read-only grant should be scoped to the collaboration task.

stem: What distinguishes a workforce tenant from an external tenant configuration?

choices.A: An external tenant is a virtual network with public IP addresses
choices.B: A workforce tenant stores only virtual disks
choices.C: An external tenant cannot authenticate people
choices.D: A workforce tenant primarily serves employees; an external tenant serves customer apps

explanations.A: It is an identity directory configuration.
explanations.B: Tenant directories manage identities and applications.
explanations.C: Authentication is a core external-tenant purpose.
explanations.D: The tenant configurations target different populations.

stem: A guest invitation is accepted successfully. What must still be considered before the guest uses a resource?

choices.A: Only the subscription's enabled state
choices.B: Only the guest object's presence in the directory
choices.C: Only the partner's successful home-directory sign-in
choices.D: The required application or resource permissions

explanations.A: An enabled subscription does not prove that this guest has access.
explanations.B: An identity object does not establish all application or resource authorization.
explanations.C: Home identity authentication does not grant the intended resource access.
explanations.D: Authentication and invitation do not automatically grant every permission.

stem: Which advantage can B2B collaboration offer compared with sharing one local account?

choices.A: Each collaborator can use an individually identifiable identity
choices.B: It eliminates the need to review guest access
choices.C: It turns guests into billing administrators
choices.D: It automatically removes every Conditional Access requirement

explanations.A: Individual identities improve access accountability.
explanations.B: External access still needs lifecycle governance.
explanations.C: Collaboration access is unrelated to automatic billing authority.
explanations.D: Guest sign-in can remain subject to access policies.

stem: A project with a partner has ended. Which identity-governance action is appropriate?

choices.A: Review and remove access that is no longer required
choices.B: Remove only the project's resource tags
choices.C: Change the guest's home-directory password policy
choices.D: Keep application access active because the guest can still authenticate

explanations.A: External access should end when its business purpose ends.
explanations.B: Tags do not revoke the guest's application access.
explanations.C: The organization should review its resource access rather than presume control of the partner's home identity.
explanations.D: Authentication does not justify access after the business purpose ends.

stem: A designer assumes a guest must abandon their home identity to collaborate. Which correction is appropriate?

choices.A: External ID can support guests using existing identities
choices.B: B2B requires every collaborator to use the same local employee account
choices.C: Resource-group Contributor automatically creates the guest's identity
choices.D: A managed legacy domain is required for every guest application

explanations.A: B2B allows supported external identity providers.
explanations.B: External collaboration can preserve individually identifiable identities.
explanations.C: Azure resource permissions do not create an external identity relationship.
explanations.D: Ordinary B2B collaboration does not require that legacy domain.

stem: What is the principal distinction between a business guest and a retail customer sign-in scenario?

choices.A: Guests must use employee credentials; customers can only use anonymous access
choices.B: Guests require legacy-domain join; customers require VNet peering
choices.C: Guests are directory administrators; customers are subscription Owners
choices.D: Guests collaborate with the workforce; customers use customer-facing applications

explanations.A: Supported external identities and customer authentication offer other designs.
explanations.B: These infrastructure requirements do not define the identity scenarios.
explanations.C: Neither identity population automatically receives those privileged roles.
explanations.D: The audience and tenant configuration differ.

stem: A guest has a valid sign-in but gets an application access denial. What is the most useful first check?

choices.A: Whether the guest has the intended application access
choices.B: Whether the app's resource group has a delete lock
choices.C: Whether the subscription has an allowed-regions policy
choices.D: Whether the guest has a larger VM quota

explanations.A: A successful identity check does not prove application authorization.
explanations.B: A resource deletion lock does not authorize guest app use.
explanations.C: Deployment-location governance does not supply application access.
explanations.D: Compute capacity does not grant access to the enterprise application.

stem: Which practice gives external collaboration a clear access boundary?

choices.A: Granting every guest every employee application
choices.B: Using one shared partner administrator account
choices.C: Treating invitation emails as permanent blanket authorization
choices.D: Assigning only the resources needed for the agreed task

explanations.A: That grants unnecessary access.
explanations.B: Shared accounts weaken accountability and scoping.
explanations.C: An invitation is not blanket authorization.
explanations.D: Scoped permissions limit exposure.

stem: How should a learner demonstrate external identity design in this lab?

choices.A: Enable paid customer-identity features during assessment
choices.B: Publish a list of real guests in the repository
choices.C: Invite arbitrary addresses to the production tenant
choices.D: Classify synthetic collaboration cases without inviting real users

explanations.A: The assessment does not require paid onboarding.
explanations.B: Real identity data should not become public learning evidence.
explanations.C: That creates unapproved external access.
explanations.D: The exercise teaches selection without changing the tenant.

stem: Which data belongs in an external-access decision record?

choices.A: Only the storage redundancy choice
choices.B: Only the Azure billing scope
choices.C: Only the home tenant's display name
choices.D: The collaborator's task and required access scope

explanations.A: Durability selection does not define the external access task.
explanations.B: Billing scope alone does not describe the collaborator's required application permissions.
explanations.C: A tenant label does not specify the authorized task and scope.
explanations.D: Business purpose and scope guide authorization.

stem: A company offers an app to many unaffiliated consumers. What makes an external tenant more suitable than workforce guest invitations for that design?

choices.A: It deploys application servers automatically
choices.B: It is configured for customer-app identity experiences
choices.C: It guarantees all app data is publicly accessible
choices.D: It removes all responsibility for protecting user data

explanations.A: Identity configuration does not automatically host the app.
explanations.B: Customer identity and workforce collaboration are distinct scenarios.
explanations.C: Authentication does not make application data public.
explanations.D: The organization still has data-protection duties.

stem: Which statement correctly describes Microsoft Entra External ID at a fundamentals level?

choices.A: It is a DNS resolver for external websites
choices.B: It supports secure access for people outside an organization
choices.C: It is a replacement for Azure Storage redundancy
choices.D: It is a billing discount for every Azure resource

explanations.A: DNS resolution is unrelated to identity collaboration.
explanations.B: External identities include partner and customer scenarios.
explanations.C: Storage redundancy addresses durability.
explanations.D: Identity services do not define universal resource discounts.
